question: An engineer updated firmware on Fabric Interconnects and activates it. However, the endpoint fails to boot from the new firmware image. What is expected to occur in this case?
options: The system defaults to and boots into kickstart image
The system defaults to and boots into GOLD firmware image
The system defaults to the GOLD firmware image
The system defaults to the backup image version
theory: Cisco UCS fabric interconnects keep a backup firmware image specifically to guard against a bad activation: if a newly activated firmware image fails to boot the endpoint, the system automatically falls back to the previous, known-good backup image version rather than defaulting to a kickstart or GOLD (factory recovery) image. This automatic fallback behavior is what protects the fabric interconnect from being left in an unbootable state after a failed firmware activation. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 14 — UCS Firmware Updates, Fabric Interconnect Firmware)
